learning_outcomes.text: Students can understand the basic principles of Nuclear Physics related to Fission and Fusion.
They can correctly identify the different parts and systems of nuclear reactors and understand their operation.
They can develop their own criteria to objectively assess whether radiation exposure poses a risk and suggest measures for its minimization.
Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
Know how to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Be able to integrate knowledge and deal with the complexity of forming judgments from information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Know how to communicate their conclusions and knowledge and the ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Possess the skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that must be, to a large extent, self-directed or autonomous.
Acquire the ability to solve problems in new or unfamiliar environments within multidisciplinary contexts related to energy engineering.
Achieve the ability to integrate knowledge to formulate applications for the development of new energy technologies.

Acquire the autonomous learning ability that allows them to continue studying by developing the capacity to search for specialized documentation in cutting-edge scientific-technical literature and its assimilation.
Assessment and application of advanced technologies for thermoelectric generation with minimum pollutant emissions.

syllabus_topics: Unit 1 – Basic concepts of Nuclear Physics.

Lesson 1. Basic concepts of Nuclear Physics: atomic structure – isotopes – binding energy per nucleon – alpha, beta and gamma radiation – concepts of activity, disintegration period, disintegration chain and radioactive equilibrium.
Lesson 2. Interaction of radiation with matter: interaction of charged particles with matter – interaction of gamma photons with matter – neutron interactions: fission and fusion-

Lesson 3. Basic concepts about nuclear reactors: chain reaction – classification of neutrons by speed – critical fission energy – effective cross-section – critical mass – effective multiplication constant – reactivity.
Lesson 4. Pressurized Water Reactors (PWR): General characteristics – Core components: Fuel Element, Vessel, Pressurizer, Steam Generator, Coolant Pump – Power Control Systems.
Lesson 5. Boiling Water Reactors (BWR): General characteristics – Core components: Fuel Element, Vessel, Steam Generator, Recirculation System, Drywell and Wetwell – Power Control Systems.

Lesson 6. Introduction to Radiological Protection: Objectives of RP – Effects of radiation on the organism: stochastic and deterministic effects – External and internal irradiation: factors determining danger – Routes of incorporation into the organism – Dose Limitation System.
Lesson 7. Basic concepts of dosimetry: Dose – Types and units – Dose Limits – Surveillance – Annual Incorporation Limits
Practical 1: Introduction to the use of the Geiger-Müller counter. Characteristic Curve.
Practical 2: Calculation of the dead time of the Geiger-Müller counter.
Practical 3: Attenuation of gamma radiation with matter.

assessment_methods.method: Exercises or small assignments during the course (classroom participation)

assessment_rules: For ordinary and extraordinary calls, the final grade is calculated as (0.70 x Exam (T)) + (0.05 x Participation in Class (TP)) + (0.25 x Practical Exam (P)), provided a minimum of 4.5 out of 10 is achieved in the theoretical exam. Practical exam and participation notes are carried over to the extraordinary call. For differentiated evaluation, the exam accounts for 90% and a course project for 10% of the grade, with no minimum required on the exam.
